clauses.requirement: For conducted emission measurements of the rear lamp electronics in the 0.15 to 30 MHz range (UN R10 Annex 19), the spectrum analyser shall comply with Table 1: peak detector RBW at -3 dB 9/10 kHz, minimum scan time 10 s/MHz; quasi-peak detector RBW at -6 dB 9 kHz, minimum scan time 200 s/MHz; average detector RBW at -3 dB 9/10 kHz, minimum scan time 10 s/MHz; if a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the RBW.

If a scanning receiver is used for conducted emission measurements in the 0.15 to 30 MHz range, it shall comply with Table 2: peak detector BW at -6 dB 9 kHz, maximum step size 5 kHz, minimum dwell time 50 ms; quasi-peak detector BW 9 kHz, maximum step size 5 kHz, minimum dwell time 1 s; average detector BW 9 kHz, maximum step size 5 kHz, minimum dwell time 50 ms; test requirements follow in section 4.

The conducted emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 0.15 to 30 MHz for measurements performed in a shielded enclosure, an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an open area test site (OATS).

Measurements shall be performed with average and either quasi-peak or peak detectors; the limits are those of Table 16 of paragraph 7.13.2.1 of UN R10 for AC lines and Table 17 of paragraph 7.13.2.2 for DC lines; if peak detectors are used, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.

Where the electronic sub-assembly is tested in the configuration 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid' (floor-standing equipment), the test setup shall follow Figure 1: ESA under test on an insulating support, charging harness, grounded AMN(s) or DC-charging-AN(s), power mains socket, measuring receiver and ground plane.

For type approval of the lamp, all definitions given in the latest series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 48 in force at the time of application for type approval shall apply, unless otherwise specified in UN R148 or in the pertinent installation UN Regulations Nos. 53, 74 and 86.

Lamps shall be treated as 'lamps of different types' when they differ in essential respects: (a) trade name or mark (same mark by different manufacturers = different types; same manufacturer differing only by trade name or mark = same type); (b) characteristics of the optical system (intensity levels, light distribution angles, inclusion or elimination of components altering optical effects by reflection, refraction, absorption and/or deformation during operation, etc.); (c) category or categories of light source(s) and/or specific identification code(s) of light source module(s); (d) lamp category, if any; (e) variable intensity control, if any; (f) sequential activation of light sources, if any. Direction indicators activated in different modes without modification of optical characteristics are not of different types; a change of colour of the light source or of any filter is not a change of type; use of LED substitute light source(s) is not a change of type, however paragraph 4.8.1.6 applies.
Any component 'being part of the lamp' shall be either physically included in the lamp body, or external (separated or not) and declared by the applicant as part of the lamp system.
